chapter: Louis Armstrong, King Oliver and St. Louis memories
title: Babe's first records with Clarence Williams
summary: Babe recalls her first recordings in 1938 for Clarence Williams, made with Connie Berry and Cozy, and Joe talks about taping tunes at home.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: (something about butter beans and smelling them)
We had the appreciation of Louis and he knew it. Like Butterbeans and Susie said...

Have the flowers when you could smell them. Well, we had a situation happen ... I didn't know too much about it and Babe and I had gotten a little tape recorder and put out our records. She loved Louis. She loved Louis musically and so we wanted to tape our tunes so we recorded together just
some things for Q.R.S., you remember? And, she did some things individually with Connie Barry and Cozy and the organist. BT: Dan Baker, organist
Oh, yeah. Really the first recording I ever made.
And Clarence Williams I can't pass by easily because I think he's one of the great ones. But, he selected her.
Oh, when would this be, Babe?
